correctness.rationale: Proof steps in RESULT.md independently establish both directions of the effective-root equivalence: a pair of white private vertices is a permanent obstruction; with at most one white per private clique, active roots can be completed locally because each private clique has size at least two; each legal base root force lifts; and a non-effective root cannot be activated internally before a root-to-root base force, so any successful decorated process projects to a base zero-forcing process. The weights \(x^{s_v}(x+s_v+1)\) and \(s_vx^{s_v-1}\) enumerate disjoint local patterns, giving the full formal identity. Uniform substitution, coefficients, minimum-degree count and injectivity follow by exact algebra. Standalone verify.py was executed from its actual bundled path and passed 624824 direct subset comparisons on 221 graphs plus 1230 coefficient comparisons. Small finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof. Counterexample for \(s=1\) defines the sharp excluded boundary.

value.rationale: The original motivating counting question is the full distribution, not the known scalar zero-forcing number. The theorem is not a small special case or isolated coefficient: it provides a genuine graph-operation transfer for all finite simple base graphs and arbitrary heterogeneous private-clique sizes, a complete combinatorial iff-classification of valid initial sets, exact every-degree counts, explicit minimum-set multiplicity, and preservation/reflection of zero-forcing-polynomial equivalence.
